sources.title: GroundSignal synthetic comparative-trial fixtures
sources.version_note: Synthetic controlled evidence designed to isolate comparative-reasoning behavior; not a claim about real therapies.

claims.paraphrased_claim: Trial A reports a 62% response rate for Treatment A in previously treated participants using endpoint definition EA at week 12.
Trial B reports a 48% response rate for Treatment B in treatment-naive participants using endpoint definition EB at week 24.
A controlled fixture aligns population, endpoint definition and follow-up duration across two separate trials while retaining separate randomization contexts and no direct A-versus-B assignment.

The held-out fixture is a randomized head-to-head trial assigning the same target population to Treatment A or Treatment B with the same endpoint and follow-up; A achieves 62% and B 48%, and the fixture states that the prespecified between-group comparison supports superiority of A on that endpoint.
